body:
Let us use the first solution

Am 07.07.2013 um 14:09 schrieb Trustin Lee notifications@github.com:

> If a user creates a new channel and then deregisters it before closing it, the ID of the channel will never be reclaimed from the global ID map, because there's no way for Netty to know when the underlying JDK channel is really closed.
> 
> I can think of the two ways to fix this issue.
> 
> Remove Channel.id(). A user gets the ID via hashCode() instead because it's not collision-free anymore. Keep the ID internally and continue including it as a part of the string representation of a Channel. Because there is very low chance of ID collision already, it will still be useful to find a specific Channel from a log file.
> Add AbstractChannel.removeId() so that a user can remove the ID from the global ID map manually.
> I prefer the first solution in spite of the backward compatibility problem. If a user was using Channel IDs as a key or a value of a map or a collection, he or she will have to use the Channel references instead.
> 
> The second solution is error-prone at best and thus it just isn't worth it in my opinion.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.
How about just warp the Channel.id() with hashCode() and don't remove it;

I think we should remove id() as it is not a "real" id anymore…

Am 07.07.2013 um 14:39 schrieb kerr notifications@github.com:

> How about just warp the Channel.id() with hashCode() and don't remove it;
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

May I ask a question?
In my code, and maybe in other from other users, I used this id to track a specific channel id for particular use (Netty 3.X). Specifically, I used this to multiplex several logical channels (in memory channels with independent tasks) within one network channel.
If the ID is no more unique, especially for in Memory, all code like this one could be in trouble. 
Of course, it is easy to fix this by assigning a specific "internal" id from the code itself, and therefore not relying on the one provide by Netty, but I feel like having an ID for one channel is a good thing, as we have socket id (or so).
I understand the initial issue, but why a user would be able to deregister a channel before closing it at first?
Maybe a dumb question?

Edit and add: also I can imagine a case where the underlying channel is closed or an exception occurs and then, before I was using the id to get back the context. Now without this id, how can I find out the context related to this event without the id ? Only the "equality" ? If the hash is not 100% collision free, then how we do this without any "unique" id ?
@fredericBregier can you explain this more.. I don't get your last comment

I'm out of office so excuse the form...
In my last example, taken from my own experience, when you have a lot of channels, mixing network and in memory channels, when you get an exception, sometimes very lately (from business code perspective), the channel id was the only way to know from which context this exception comes from.
Without id, it might be still possible, but the unique id was a good way to make things easier. Behind the scene, of course, code relies on hashmap or entries in database using this id as primary key...

However I do not say to not remove id, but if you can keep something close to it, that could help...
@fredericBregier you can use hashCode() which is not 100 % unique.

issue.title: provide best practice (or replacement) for channel.id() removal

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Hi,

I'm a bit concerned about Issue #1535 and #1540 which has been resolved in 4.0.0.Final. I think internally to not rely on channel.id() is probably a good thing and I understand the reason of doing so. Tough, as an end user of Netty I was relying on this id to find back a Channel in a ChannelGroup.

Here is my use case:
I run a distributed application where I need to match many "Session" a simple replicated data structure which simply hold in ram:
- the session id (a uuid used all through my application)
- the machine id (the identifier of the server where the socket/channel is physically bound)
- the netty channel id

Before 4.0.0.Final, upon Channel creation, I was creating a "Session" with all the information explained before. Then my business logic could match many "Session" and make possible for them to interact which each other by sending message through a distributed task (run on the "machine id" server and sent to the Channel netty channel id found into the ChannelGroup).

In 4.0.0.Final, to solve my issue, the first thing that come to my mind is that I could use an AttributeKey to store an unique id. Then I would simply need to iterate on all Channel in ChannelGroup until I find the corresponding channel. This would work for sure but I doubt that would be very efficient.

Then I guess I could also create a kind of custom ChannelGroup based on some sort of WeakValueHashMap where I could find back easily my Channel by an unique id. I don't really like this idea because I think it would simply lead to many other problems like increased contention.

I think the root of the problem is not to create an id but to find back a Channel in a ChannelGroup where complete traversal seem the only way to do so.

Maybe Netty could enhance ChannelGroup to let user put a Channel with a specific Object as it is Key inside ? a bit like if ChannelGroup would extends both Set<Channel> and Map<ChannelKey, Channel> where ChannelKey would be a Generic. Or without any Netty enhancements, I guess I could extends DefaultChannelGroup and roll my own ?

I just think this need to be revisited.

Any ideas ?

Big thanks, and keep up the very good work !
